confirmed.issue: Repair-vs-replace thresholds are mis-paired to their named sources. The sentence attributes BOTH the 25-30%-of-roof-area rule AND the 50%-of-replacement-cost rule to "Kellow, Modernize, and Josten Roofing." Per facts-materials-economics §8, Kellow/Modernize/Josten back ONLY the 30%-of-COST rule; the 50% rule = WeatherShield/Home Depot, and the 25%-of-AREA rule = RapidRestore/MyQuoteIQ. The brief §D states this split explicitly.
confirmed.evidence: "...replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the contractor-consensus thresholds attributed to Kellow, Modernize, and Josten Roofing."
confirmed.suggestedFix: Re-pair to the correct §8 sources. Before: "...damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the contractor-consensus thresholds attributed to Kellow, Modernize, and Josten Roofing." After: "...damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area, per RapidRestore and Kellow, or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the most widely cited threshold per WeatherShield and Home Depot."
confirmed.reasoning: The offending text is present verbatim in faqs[4].answer of src/data/combo-content/montclair/custom-roof-design-consultation.ts: "...replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the contractor-consensus thresholds attributed to Kellow, Modernize, and Josten Roofing." This is a real source-attribution mismatch against the authoritative fact pack. facts-materials-economics.md §8 (the named-source decision-rule table, lines 305-307) is unambiguous: the 50%-of-cost rule = WeatherShield/Home Depot/industry; the 25%-of-AREA rule = RapidRestore/MyQuoteIQ; and Kellow/Modernize/Josten back ONLY the 30%-of-COST rule (line 306). The Montclair sentence attributes BOTH the 25-30%-area rule AND the 50%-cost rule to Kellow/Modernize/Josten — and §8 backs neither of those two rules to those three sources. So the named-source claim is factually wrong on both counts.\n\nTwo caveats the finding overstated, neither of which refutes it: (1) The finding claims "brief §D states this split explicitly" — it does NOT; brief lines 205-208 are themselves loose, bundling "the 30% / 25%-area rule = Kellow/Modernize/Josten/RapidRestore." The authority for the split is the fact pack §8, not the brief. (2) The exact phrasing "attributed to Kellow, Modernize, and Josten" for the area+50% rules is COMMITTED GOLD (bloomfield/roof-replacement.ts, nutley/roof-replacement.ts, nutley/roof-replacement-cost.ts), and the runbook flags this as a known-LOOSE committed pattern. But "gold-consistent" does not immunize a factual mis-pin against the primary fact pack — and the project's own committed gold ALSO carries the precise re-pairing (bloomfield/storm-damage-roof-replacement.ts: "the 25% area rule per RapidRestore and MyQuoteIQ and the 50% cost rule per WeatherShield and Home Depot"), proving the accurate form is the higher standard. Per the runbook instruction to apply pack-accurate re-pairings to CONFIRMED findings, this is a fixable source-attribution defect. No Montclair fact, COA posture, entity-grounding, or third-party-credential issue is involved; the fix only relocates/re-attributes, preserving all facts.
confirmed.finalFix: In src/data/combo-content/montclair/custom-roof-design-consultation.ts, faqs[4].answer — BEFORE: "A Newark Quality Roofing consultation also models the replace-now-or-later decision: replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the contractor-consensus thresholds attributed to Kellow, Modernize, and Josten Roofing." AFTER: "A Newark Quality Roofing consultation also models the replace-now-or-later decision: replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area, the contractor-consensus threshold per RapidRestore and Kellow, or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, the most widely cited threshold per WeatherShield and Home Depot."
